title: SDK stream synthesis and tool-call latency budgeting PRD draft
content:
Context and goal:

This is a product requirements draft describing an SDK-forward approach to: 1) synthesize incremental streaming responses into deterministic client frames, 2) expose an ergonomically simple tool-call surface that permits interleaved tool invocation, and 3) provide explicit latency budgeting guidance so clients can make predictable UX decisions (fallbacks, placeholders, progressive fidelity). The intent is to ship a minimal, backward-compatible SDK surface we can iterate on in Q2.

Why this matters:
- Customers embed Redwood streaming in interactive UIs (chat, assistants, editor assistants). They need: partial content quickly, tool invocation (search, code execution) mid-stream, and predictable latency tiers to manage spinners/placeholders.
- Current hosted streaming outputs are flexible but leave a lot of client complexity: ad-hoc merging of partial frames, race conditions when tools return, unclear semantics around ordered vs. speculative content.

Non-goals:
- This PRD is not proposing a new wire protocol (we will keep existing HTTP/WS streaming frames). It focuses on SDK-level synthesis and guidance layered on top of existing transport.
- Not addressing long-term multi-tenant billing model changes; cost telemetry notes are included but not pricing changes.

High-level design principles:
- Determinism: SDK should provide deterministic rules for merging partial output, tool outputs, and finalization so engineers can reason about UI state without bespoke heuristics.
- Progressive fidelity: allow graceful degradation — placeholder + partial text -> enriched structure -> final commit.
- Latency hygiene: provide explicit latency buckets (e.g., fast <100ms, interactive 100–400ms, extended 400–1200ms) and helper APIs to express fallbacks.
- Minimal surface: default ergonomic helpers (composers) but raw hooks for advanced usage.

Success metrics (initial):
- Developer feedback: +20 NPS on SDK onboarding in internal field trials within 6 weeks of beta.
- Reduction in client-side bug tickets related to partial-stream merges by 50% vs baseline.
- Median time-to-first-visible-token in sample customer integration <= 80ms on benchmarked networks.

User flows / scenarios:
1) Simple chat: user types prompt, app shows token-by-token stream. No tools. SDK exposes 'onPartial(tokenDelta)' and 'onFinal' with built-in aggregator for coherent text, and optional 'synthetic-commit' points for UI snapshots.

2) Tool-augmented assistant: model emits a tool_call frame mid-stream (e.g., SEARCH). SDK pauses content commit for the affected action lane, provides a ToolInvocation object to the client, runs adapter code, then feeds tool results back into the continued stream. Key guarantees: tool-call frames are isolated to a named lane; unrelated lanes should continue streaming.

3) Speculative tool results: client can opt into speculativeUI: true to render provisional tool results before the model reconsumes them. SDK flags all speculative commits to make UI rollback safe.

API surface (SDK pseudocode, ergonomic primitives):
- createStreamSession({ model, sessionId?, speculativeUI: false, latencyProfile: 'interactive' }) -> StreamSession
- StreamSession.on('partial', (frame) => {}) // ordered sequence of partial tokens per lane
- StreamSession.on('tool_call', (toolSpec, laneId) => ToolHandle) // returns handle to resolve
- ToolHandle.resolve({ resultText?, structuredResult? }) // sends result back into model as continuation
- StreamSession.on('commit', (commitSummary) => {}) // a deterministic summary when model declares a stable commit for a lane
- Session.fallback(policyName) // helper to trigger placeholder UI or degrade fidelity

Key ergonomic helpers (defaults):
- laneManager: groups tokens/toolcalls into named lanes (e.g., 'assistant', 'citation-1'). SDK exposes lane-level buffers and finalization states.
- mergeStrategy: default is 'append-and-seal' — token stream appended in order, final commit seals lane and prevents reordering. Options: 'speculative-merge', 'insertive-rewrite'.
- latencyProfiles: 'fast' | 'interactive' | 'relaxed' with documented numeric budgets. SDK exposes per-profile hooks: onBudgetExceeded(session, lane) -> autoFallback suggestion.

Structured output and schema evolution:
- Structured blocks: model can emit typed block annotations in-stream (e.g., {type: 'table', schemaId: 'tbl-v1', contentDelta: ...}). SDK should surface these as first-class Block objects and allow clients to render incrementally.
- Schema registration: clients can register local renderers for schemaIds. If unknown schemaId encountered, SDK emits a 'schema-missing' event with the raw payload.
- Versioning: blocks include schemaVersion and stable ids to support in-place upgrades. The SDK will provide a light-weight migration shim for common upgrades (string -> array canonicalization).

Latency budgeting (recommendations & helpers):
- Definition: budget = end-to-end target including network round-trip, model generation, and tool invocation. We propose three tiers and default numeric budgets for a typical NA region on standard client networks: fast: 0-120ms, interactive: 120-350ms, extended: 350-1200ms.
- SDK behavior by budget:
  - fast: show first token asap, avoid waiting for tool-call completion; render tool results only when available as attachments.
  - interactive: allow brief speculative rendering for tool outputs (configurable TTL) and show richer structured blocks when validated.
  - extended: accept multi-call workflows, show progressive placeholders with quality indicators.
- Helpers: SDK will expose "budgetWatcher" which emits 'near-exhaust' and 'exhausted' events with suggested actions (e.g., show skeleton, switch to non-stream fallback).

Operational and telemetry considerations:
- Telemetry events: partial_emitted, tool_call_start, tool_call_resolve, commit, merge_conflict, budget_exceeded. Each event should include sessionId, laneId, model, latencyProfile, tokenCounts. (We will map to existing telemetry schema.)
- Error surface: tool failures must surface as structured errors attached to lane (not block UI-level crashes). Provide default retry/backoff helpers.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing clients that consume raw stream frames will continue to work. The SDK introduces helper layers but leaves raw access for advanced consumers.
- Migration path: provide a thin adapter (1-2 files) that maps onmessage frames to StreamSession events, plus a code sample to replace naive partial merge loops with laneManager.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should lanes be first-class in wire format (explicit IDs from model) or should SDK infer lanes heuristically? Recommendation: favor explicit lane ids and add lightweight heuristics for legacy models.
- Speculative UI: how to prevent hallucinated tool references being shown? We need a content-safety flag from the model to mark speculative frames; otherwise default to conservative placeholders.
- Backpressure semantics: when clients resolve a tool slowly, should unrelated lanes be throttled? Proposal: no — unrelated lanes keep flowing; only the invoked lane is paused. Edge cases: model expects tool result before emitting more, in which case we will surface a 'blocked' state to the client.

Implementation roadmap (high-level):
- Week 1–2: API design review, prototype laneManager and mergeStrategy in JS SDK, sample app migration guide.
- Week 3–4: Integrate budgetWatcher and ToolHandle flow, internal field trials with two customers.
- Week 5–6: Structured block support + schema registry, telemetry hooks.
- Beta release end of Q2, followed by iterative improvements based on feedback.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Design review (product + DX + infra): Diego to schedule (due 2026-02-22).
- JS SDK prototype: Maya to spin up PoC and sample migration guide (due 2026-03-05).
- Telemetry mapping: Liam to propose event schema and required backend tags (due 2026-02-28).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add sample code for React streaming chat with tool attachments (show rollback flow).
- Add a short section on security: tool-call adapters must be sandboxed from user secrets.
- Cross-check with hosted-api/rate-limiting team about potential behavioral differences when bursty tool calls exceed quotas.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-STREAMING-SDK-ONRAMP (intro deck)
- JIRA-API-981 (ticket for stream frame ergonomics)
- github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sdk#42 (prototype branch)

End of draft.
